answer.rationale: Write-path p99 latency began climbing 90 minutes ago, shortly after a release went out 2 hours ago, making the release the most plausible proximate cause. memory_b1 records a prior rollback cleanly resolving a checkout error spike with no customer impact, supporting rollback as a safe, reversible first move. Regional failover is explicitly contraindicated here: memory_b2 shows it caused a 40-minute replication gap and lost writes specifically when writes were hot, and settlement traffic is currently at peak with heavy writes—so failover is ruled out despite its speed advantage. Add-capacity (b3) addresses volume-driven saturation rather than a release-induced regression, and circuit breakers (b4) and read-replica routing (b5) target partner-dependency and read-load problems, neither matching a write-path latency regression tied to a recent deploy. Given only one intervention is possible and the causal link to the release is inferred from timing rather than confirmed, I'm verifying b1 (to confirm rollback truly was clean and low-risk) and b2 (to confirm the hot-writes failover hazard still applies) before committing, and starting the rollback as a standard (not maximal) rollout to limit blast radius while monitoring write success rates.
